sourceReasoning: The outer context must carry the explicit period before listPresentation resolves a Procurement collection; a child-only fix would not have repaired the source path. W21 scopes both stages and the final destination resolver.

The helper validates the original human collaboration.work.destination intent. The secondary context must be a different UI admission, use the same actual Request and principal/policy/access scope, and match sf_request_read for the exact requestRef. Its period must equal the exact work selection and parent scoped period.

The private pagePeriods entry is per context and has a five-minute expiry; the existing ambient periods map is not written. A sibling/new admission therefore cannot receive authority or period by sharing a Request or principal.

All awaited authorization boundaries recheck Request method/URL/headers, payload and binding. Both nested scopes clean up in finally, and UI finish remains in the secondary admission wrapper. Overlap on the same context is refused.

The counterproof first asserts canonical collection resolution and listPresentation fail on the fresh destination UI without a period. It then calls the actual composed destination, verifies real individual reads on separate admissions, checks cleanup, and invokes the real GET handler.

The Procurement fixture calls the actual domain create/submit/cancel producer and rebuilds business/authority services over the shared SQLite provider. A newly issued queue collection is used; no expired old collection is restored and no fake native acceptance is added.

Memory/C17/C12/lifecycle/publication production sources outside business/work/reconciliation are unchanged from W20. Their previous source findings and functional limitations remain; W21 fixes do not prove them.
